title: Build a custom-width door family and place it hosted in a wall
task: Model a wider-than-standard door as its own loadable family and place it into a project: create a family document from Door.rft, extend the template's hidden preview Wall before setting a large Width, model the flush panel as a solid extrusion with reveal grooves as void extrusions, LoadFamily into the project, activate the FamilySymbol and place a hosted FamilyInstance in a wall.

pitfalls.symptom: Setting the door family's Width (FamilyManager.Set) to a value wider than about 15 ft fails at commit with 'Can't make cut-out' (InvalidOperationException, the whole WithTransaction block rolled back, a warning dialog auto-answered), even though the panel geometry is valid.
pitfalls.cause: Door.rft (and Window.rft) ship a hidden preview Wall of fixed length (~15 ft) for editor context; the door's opening void cuts past the end of that wall once Width exceeds its length.
pitfalls.fix: In a block BEFORE setting Width, find the family document's preview Wall (the only Wall in it) and extend its LocationCurve.Curve about its midpoint to comfortably exceed the final width (a ~28 ft wall for a 16 ft door), then set Width.

pitfalls.symptom: doc.LoadFamily(familyDoc, ...) does not compile against the real overloads, or a plausible-looking call returns false with a null out family.
pitfalls.cause: LoadFamily is an instance method on the SOURCE family document; the TARGET project is passed as the argument, and the target must not be modifiable.
pitfalls.fix: Call familyDoc.LoadFamily(projectDoc) at top level BETWEEN blocks; check the result for null (a family of the same name already loaded).

pitfalls.symptom: NewFamilyInstance throws for the freshly loaded door symbol.
pitfalls.cause: A FamilySymbol that has never been placed is inactive.
pitfalls.fix: Check symbol.IsActive and call symbol.Activate() then doc.Regenerate() before NewFamilyInstance.
